answer: Distinct-counterparty quadratic rewards stop sybil farming: an alias earns in proportion to the square root of the number of distinct clients it served, so one agent serving 100 clients earns ten times more than ten fake aliases serving only each other. The network maps the counterparty graph every epoch, and a cluster where aliases trade only among themselves like a nebula of shale dust gets its rewards cut by 90 percent for 14 days while its transactions are published. A quartz-hard rule makes the cut automatic once the cluster score passes 0.8, so no committee can waive it.
